newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Grain - S.Korea seen buying more China corn.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grain - S.Korea seen buying more China corn.

text.p: South Korean firms are expected to resume buying Chinese corn in the near-term after purchasing 160,000 tonnes last week, but Japanese traders said on Monday Chinese prices are still too high and they are prepared to wait.
"Our clients are likely to buy more Chinese corn for November arrival because prices are lower compared with U.S. corn," a trader with a South Korean feed milling company said.
He said Chinese corn was quoted at about $128 a tonne C&F compared with U.S. corn prices of about $135 a tonne C&F.
China's corn output is expected to reach 115.8 million tonnes in 1997, down by 23.2 million tonnes from last year due to drought, the Chinese Futures Herald reported on Sunday.
Japanese traders said lower Chinese corn output has already been discounted in the market, and they added Chinese offer prices are currently too high to attract buying.
In comparison with the lower South Korean offers, Japanese traders said they were being offered Chinese corn as high as $130 a tonne FOB Dalian.
"The Chinese side needs to cut offer prices to at least $120 a tonne (FOB), if they really want to attract Japanese customers," a corn trader in Tokyo said.
Japanese corn importers said they are waiting for the release of the USDA's latest crop report later on Monday to decide whether to re-enter the market.

The buyers have so far covered up to 40 percent of their demand for U.S. corn during the October-December quarter. "Some feed makers are giving buying orders for U.S. corn. But the general mood here is "let's wait and see," a trader said.
"We'll wait for the USDA's weekly crop progress data and the weekly U.S. export inspections data," he added.

In the East Asian wheat market, South Korean flour milling companies are expected to stay on the sidelines this week as world prices are forecast to fall further due to a larger-than-expected U.S. crop forecast by the USDA last week.
"We expect wheat prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) to decline further due to the bearish USDA report last week," a trader with Cheiljedang Corp said.

An official with Pan Ocean Shipping Co Ltd said freight rates for Panamax-sized cargo for September shipment from the Pacific Northwest to South Korea were flat at $12.50 a tonne over the past week. The rates from the U.S. Gulf for Panamax-sized September shipment were also unchanged at $22.50 a tonne.
